subject.title: Output sanitizer: improve duplicate detection for same-line and partial duplicates

question: How broad should OpenClaw's user-facing output sanitizer be allowed to get when removing partial or near-duplicate assistant text?
rationale: The concrete glued final-tag repeat is source-reproducible, but broad substring or near-duplicate cleanup can delete intentional user-requested repetition.

options.title: Conservative adjacent-only repair
options.body: Handle the reported glued final-tag repeat plus exact adjacent same-line or single-newline duplicates with focused false-positive tests.

options.title: Broader partial-duplicate sanitizer
options.body: Allow substring or near-duplicate removal, accepting higher false-positive risk and requiring stronger preservation tests.

options.title: Wait for broad normalizer PR
options.body: Defer until the larger visible-output normalizer pull request has a settled owner-approved shape.

recommendation.title: Conservative adjacent-only repair
recommendation.body: Handle the reported glued final-tag repeat plus exact adjacent same-line or single-newline duplicates with focused false-positive tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter is the strongest routing candidate from sanitizer introduction history and prior issue review context.
